monthly_review.summary: You've increased volume and intensity this month, with notable gains in pace and cadence, though aerobic efficiency and HR zone distribution show signs of shifting effort toward higher intensities.
monthly_review.highlight: Your Zone 3 time increased from 19% to 28% while Zone 2 dropped from 43% to 30%, indicating a meaningful shift toward threshold-intensity work — a positive sign of progressing training stress, but one requiring careful recovery monitoring.

goal_tracker.message: You’ve already exceeded last month’s total distance (54.5 km vs. 46.0 km) and matched the number of runs (10), so no additional runs or km are needed to meet last month’s baseline — you’re ahead on volume and pace.

insights.title: Efficiency improved despite faster paces
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.42 to 13.55 while average pace improved by 12 sec/km and average HR increased by 4 bpm — suggesting better neuromuscular coordination and metabolic economy at higher intensities.

insights.title: Zone 3 dominance signals threshold focus
insights.body: Zone 3 contribution jumped from 19% (May) to 28% (June), while Zone 2 dropped from 43% to 30% — confirming intentional progression into lactate threshold work, consistent with your recent long runs averaging 9:27–9:42 min/km at 140–144 bpm.

insights.title: Cadence surge correlates with pace improvement
insights.body: Average cadence increased +5 spm (146 → 151), and your fastest recent run (Jun 11: 6:32 min/km, 162 spm) shows you can sustain high turnover — yet stride length dropped from 91 cm (easy run) to 68–72 cm in longer efforts, suggesting form adaptation under fatigue.

insights.title: Low-effort run shows under-recovery signal
insights.body: On Jun 19 (10:50 min/km, 112 bpm), your aerobic TE was only 1.6 — the lowest in recent logs — and ground contact time spiked to 344 ms (vs. 314–322 ms in other June runs), indicating possible residual fatigue or insufficient recovery before that session.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a strict Zone 2 aerobic builder: 6.5 km at 128–134 bpm (per your HR zones), cadence ≥148 spm, targeting ground contact <320 ms.
recommendations.reason: Your Zone 2 time fell to 30% this month (from 43% last month), and your Jun 19 low-TE run suggests accumulated fatigue — rebuilding Zone 2 capacity will support sustainable threshold development.

recommendations.action: Insert one 10-min barefoot or minimalist strides post-run this week: 8 × 15-sec fast leg cycles (focus on quick turnover, light ground contact), emphasizing knee lift and relaxed arms.
recommendations.reason: Cadence improved but vertical oscillation remains steady (7.2–8.4 cm); targeted neuromuscular drills will reinforce efficiency gains without adding load.

recommendations.action: After your next long run (>9 km), perform 3 × 60-sec single-leg balance holds (eyes open → eyes closed) on each leg, focusing on quiet ankle control.
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time increased by ~40 ms during your slowest recent run (344 ms), correlating with reduced stability cues — this drill directly addresses neuromuscular control under fatigue.

weekly_focus.description: Reinforce aerobic foundation and neuromuscular control to support continued threshold progress without compromising recovery or form integrity.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 aerobic builder (6.5 km, HR 128–134 bpm)
Threshold cruise (4 × 1.2 km @ 9:00–9:15 min/km, 90-sec jog recovery)
Recovery + form session (3 km easy + 10-min stride drills + balance work)
